scope: Public articles and historical records about Jim Brewer, the Brewer family companies and their Bricktown projects. Growing archive, not an exhaustive inventory.

articles.title: Bricktown rides antique shuttle
articles.summary: Jim Brewer supported a proposed antique-car shuttle linking downtown parking with Bricktown. The report captures parking pressure and the push to diversify the district beyond nightlife.

articles.title: City Beat: Schwartz elected president
articles.summary: A brief mention places Jim Brewer on an Oklahoma City delegation to San Antonio and credits his influence on the proposed canal alignment along California Street.

articles.title: Depot renovation begins for return of Amtrak
articles.summary: Coverage of approved federal funding and restoration preparations at the Santa Fe Depot. Jim Brewer discussed the work needed before passenger rail service returned.

articles.title: Restoring our gateway
articles.summary: Jim and Brent Brewer’s plans for the Santa Fe Depot combined passenger facilities with preservation of its Art Deco character. This is a contemporary account of the restoration effort.

articles.title: OKC gets rail passenger link to Texas
articles.summary: An account of preparations for renewed passenger service, including Brewer Enterprises’ restoration work at the Santa Fe Depot.

articles.title: Bricktown: a hub of Oklahoma City history
articles.summary: A canal-opening-era history of the warehouse district describes Jim Brewer’s property investments during the 1980s within Bricktown’s broader redevelopment story.

articles.title: Heartland Flyer anniversary preparations
articles.summary: A preview of the train’s first-anniversary celebrations mentions Jim Brewer hosting a special luncheon. The article documents plans rather than confirming every event occurred.

articles.title: Pioneering Bricktown
articles.summary: Looks back at early investment and entertainment in Bricktown, including Jim Brewer’s involvement from 1985. It also recognizes the other developers and businesses involved in the district’s revival.

articles.title: Bricktown construction booms
articles.summary: Jim Brewer discusses the effect of MAPS investment and new construction. The report also describes uneven weekday activity as the entertainment district continued to develop.

articles.title: Jim and Patsy Brewer parking-lot sale
articles.summary: A property-transactions roundup reports Jim and Patsy Brewer selling a parking lot near Sheridan and Joe Carter for a proposed Bricktown Market Place development. The apartment sale in the original headline is a separate transaction.

articles.title: Celebrate the Fourth at Red, White and Boom!
articles.summary: C.J. Macklin previews Brewer Entertainment’s free, three-day celebration with the Oklahoma City Philharmonic and other performers. This event was at Downtown Airpark, separate from Bricktown’s earlier fireworks celebrations.

articles.title: These Walls: Santa Fe Station
articles.summary: Traces the station’s architecture and later uses, including Jim Brewer’s 1998 purchase, restoration, and the return of passenger service in 1999.

articles.title: Bricktown’s 13th annual blues festival
articles.summary: Jake Dalton previews the free Blues & BBQ event at Sheridan and Oklahoma avenues, featuring Marcia Ball, Bugs Henderson, and regional musicians. This report documents the festival and lineup; it does not establish the complete production credits.

articles.title: Bricktown Comprehensive Parking Strategy
articles.summary: The city’s parking study lists Jim Brewer among consulted stakeholders and Bricktown Parking Investors among contacted operators. It documents district parking conditions; it does not by itself establish the relationship between every similarly named parking business.

articles.title: Bricktown pioneer Jim Brewer dies
articles.summary: Remembers Jim Brewer’s investments, venues, festivals, and prominent role in Bricktown. Alongside tributes, the account describes a strong personality and disagreements with others involved in the district.

articles.title: Jim Brewer obituary
articles.summary: The family obituary recounts Jim’s early businesses, oil ventures, and work in Bricktown. Originally published November 12–13, 2008, it provides a family remembrance alongside independent newspaper coverage.

articles.title: Bricktown merchant mourns district pioneer
articles.summary: Scott Cooper records Jim Cowan’s memories of Brewer, the merchants’ association, and major crowds at the 1999 Fourth of July celebration. It connects the events to Bricktown’s changing fortunes.

articles.title: “Mayor of Bricktown” dies
articles.summary: A remembrance of Jim Brewer’s business career and the entertainment ventures that helped bring visitors into the warehouse district.

articles.title: Coca-Cola Bricktown Events Center directory entry
articles.summary: The 2008 venue guide lists Brewer Entertainment with the Coca-Cola Bricktown Events Center at 425 California. This contemporaneous industry record helps document the venue’s earlier name.

articles.title: Bricktown merchants hold talks on future
articles.summary: A Chamber-hosted newspaper report covers merchants’ discussions about Bricktown’s next phase, including plans to honor early contributors such as Neal Horton and Jim Brewer.
articles.author: Steve Lackmeyer

articles.title: Alea London v. Canal Club
articles.publisher: Oklahoma Court of Civil Appeals / Justia
articles.summary: An insurance-coverage appeal arising from an intoxicated-driver injury case. The opinion records that claims against Brewer Entertainment and Bricktown Canal Properties were dismissed without prejudice before the underlying trial.
articles.context: The appeal concerned coverage for a judgment against Canal Club, not a liability finding against the Brewer companies. The appellate court reversed and remanded for judgment in the insurer’s favor. Dismissal without prejudice is not a decision on the merits.

articles.title: Santa Fe Station’s hidden architecture
articles.summary: Ben Fenwick examines a long-hidden tunnel beneath the tracks and the station’s potential as a transportation hub. Brent Brewer discusses the building as city planning work continues.

articles.title: Oklahoma officials reach Amtrak pact
articles.summary: An AP report describes a station-use agreement following locked-door incidents that required alternative arrangements for passengers. Brent Brewer said repeated requests for a new lease had gone unanswered.
articles.context: The report documents a subsequent agreement with the state. Summary is based on indexed text of the newspaper preserved by Texas Tech’s archive.

articles.title: The Rising
articles.summary: Lindsey Johnson explores Oklahoma City’s urban renewal and MAPS-era development. Jim Brewer’s entertainment investments appear within the larger story of downtown’s transformation.

articles.title: Western World Insurance v. Markel American Insurance
articles.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals, Tenth Circuit / Justia
articles.summary: The opinion describes an employee’s fall down an elevator shaft at the Bricktown Haunted House and the resulting suit against Brewer Entertainment. The injury suit had already settled; this appeal concerned the insurers’ responsibility for costs.
articles.context: The court reversed summary judgment for Markel and remanded. This was an insurance-allocation decision, not a new injury judgment against Brewer Entertainment.

articles.title: Bass pros and cons
articles.summary: A debate over government incentives for retail development includes Brent Brewer’s support for anchor stores and cautions about public subsidies. The disagreement concerns development policy.

articles.title: Festival of the foods
articles.summary: Greg Elwell’s Festival of the Arts food coverage includes Brewer Entertainment’s brisket sales. It documents food operations at the Arts Council’s festival, rather than crediting Brewer with producing the entire event.

articles.title: Mystery train
articles.summary: Jerry Bohnen reports on the city’s effort to acquire the Santa Fe Depot and a sharp gap between the owner’s asking price and the city’s offer. The article captures an unresolved acquisition dispute at that time.

articles.title: Grant and valuation move transit hub forward
articles.summary: A follow-up covers federal grant funding and a reported $4.5 million depot valuation in the condemnation process. This is a dated account of that process, not a statement of the final acquisition price.

articles.title: The Scare is Everywhere Inside the Bricktown Haunted Warehouse
articles.summary: Brewer Entertainment announces the attraction’s 28th annual season at the Pepsi Chevy Bricktown Events Center, 425 California. This company-issued release documents the venue name and advertised season.

articles.title: Seeing red, gold and green
articles.summary: Caele Pemberton reports on Brewer Entertainment’s long-running free Reggae Fest. Alongside performers and community appeal, the account discusses weather risk and years when the event lost money.

articles.title: New life for haunted house site
articles.summary: Molly M. Fleming covers Brent and Brett Brewer’s building renovations honoring Jim. The article also describes debate over electronic signs and advertising rules in the historic district.
articles.context: Renovation approval and unresolved sign questions are separate issues. The report does not establish a final denial of every Brewer sign proposal.

articles.title: The scare house that helped revive a warehouse district
articles.summary: Brett Fieldcamp interviews Brent Brewer about the Haunted Warehouse’s origins, its early crowds, and the creative work behind its scares. Recollections and attendance figures are presented as the interviewee’s account.

articles.title: Reggaefest becomes a summertime tradition
articles.summary: Ben Luschen previews the festival’s 21st edition and interviews Brent Brewer about its free, all-ages format and place in Bricktown’s summer calendar.

articles.title: Debating the Bricktown octopus mural
articles.summary: Patrick’s commentary examines criticism and changing responses to Jack Fowler’s octopus mural, a project supported by the Brewers and Downtown OKC Initiatives. It is included as an opinion piece, rather than an objective verdict on the artwork.

articles.title: Wormy Dog Saloon to close its doors
articles.summary: Jacob McCleland and Ted Streuli discuss the venue’s closure. The account says Levelland Productions chose not to renew its lease with property owner Brewer Entertainment; Brent Brewer was assessing the building’s future.

articles.title: Alcoholmanac: Spirited tradition
articles.summary: Matt Dinger interviews Brent Brewer about O’Brien’s March 17, 1990 opening and the family’s St. Patrick’s Day tradition. Its 2020 event plans are a preview, not confirmation that the celebration took place.

articles.title: Bricktown funding request
articles.summary: Brent Brewer calls for more funding as Bricktown grows.

articles.title: Bricktown Collection
articles.summary: A collection of photographs and district history, including family-contributed material and the work of multiple early developers. A starting point for placing the Brewer story in its wider setting.

articles.title: Bricktown history
articles.summary: The district’s history page describes its warehouse origins and early entertainment attractions, including the Haunted Warehouse associated with Jim Brewer.

articles.title: Oklahoma City Santa Fe Depot
articles.summary: The station history documents the depot’s architecture, Jim Brewer’s 1998 purchase, and the return of passenger rail service in 1999.

articles.title: Bricktown Okctopus mural
articles.summary: The state tourism listing identifies Jack Fowler’s large Bricktown octopus mural. It provides a descriptive record alongside the archive’s coverage of public reactions to the artwork.

articles.title: Bricktown parking debate stirs up
articles.publisher: The Oklahoman / copy preserved on OKCTalk
articles.summary: A newspaper article attributed to Steve Lackmeyer describes merchants’ complaints about parking prices and control of public lots. The copied report says Jim Brewer declined comment, while the Bricktown Association argued that cheaper parking options needed better publicity.
articles.context: The surviving copy was posted July 21, 2007; the original publisher page was not located. The city’s 2008 parking study independently identifies this article and the related discussion. This entry summarizes the attributed newspaper text, not forum replies.
articles.author: Steve Lackmeyer (attributed in preserved copy)
